title: The Work I Might Have Chosen

collection.credit: NEW EVENTS — INNER LIFE, PART VIII (141-160, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)

ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it)

collection.description: Mending a fishing net, a villager wonders what life would be like if they had chosen different work.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is mending a fishing net, the way (subject.he/she) has done most days for years, when a thought sneaks up on (subject.him/her): what if (subject.he/she) had picked something else? A healer, maybe. A builder. A storyteller, traveling from village to village. Would (subject.he/she) be happier? Would (subject.he/she) be the same person at all?

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (subject) keeps mending. (subject.He/She) doesn't come to any conclusion. Some of the other lives sound wonderful. Some sound exhausting. This one is (subject.his/her) own, knots and all. It's not the only life (subject.he/she) could have had. It's the one (subject.he/she) has. (subject.He/She) ties off the last knot and decides that's alright, today at least.

a__fx.name: Answer A
a__fx.text: (friend), it turns out, has wondered the same thing. (friend.He/She) always thought (friend.he/she) might have been a fisher. They laugh about it, then get quieter. "I think I'd still be me," says (subject), finally. "Just with different calluses." (friend) holds up (friend.his/her) hands. They compare calluses. It's a strangely nice way to end the conversation.
